title: MWR Output Artifact
description: The complete, structured output of the Messages Worth Receiving (MWR) gate. MWR consumes one FHC output artifact and returns, per in-scope segment, a binary verdict: can a PVP-grade message be built from this segmentation work, yes or no. 'yes' carries an exemplar message as evidence; 'no' carries a named gap. Governed by MWR_CONSTITUTION.md v1.3.

mwr_version.description: Version of the MWR constitution this run was graded against. Example: 1.3

source_artifact.description: Identifying metadata copied from the consumed FHC artifact, so a verdict is traceable to the exact input it judged.

source_agent.description: FHC artifact's source_agent. Example: FHC v0.5 Beta

scope_used.description: Which tier the gate ran over. Gold by default; Silver or Bronze only under explicit override, and override replaces Gold scope, it does not add to it (constitution Section 3).

override.description: True when the user overrode the default Gold scope. When true, every entry in segment_verdicts that carries an exemplar must carry override_warning.

run_decline.description: Present ONLY for a run-level (brand-profile) decline. Per constitution Section 6: when brand_profile.value_prop or differentiator is empty, every segment fails Standard 2 identically, so the gate returns ONE run-level decline instead of N identical per-segment 'no's. When present, segment_verdicts is empty.

reason.description: Plain statement of the brand-level gap. Example: brand profile incomplete: value_prop missing, no segment can clear Standard 2 until supplied.

missing_fields.description: Which MWR-critical brand_profile fields are empty.

segment_verdicts.description: One verdict per in-scope segment. Empty when run_decline is present.

allOf.description: Either the run declined at the brand level (run_decline present, no segment verdicts) or it produced per-segment verdicts (no run_decline).

standard_check.description: The grader's yes/no on a single Gold Standard. No partial credit. Every 'met: true' must cite the basis that earns it; for Standards 3, 6, and 7 the basis must rest on a 'public'-classed source that survives the two mechanical hardening checks.

basis.description: On 'met: true', the specific fact/field (and its access_class where the standard requires public) that earns the yes. On 'met: false', why it misses.

recommended.description: Carried through from the FHC segment, if present.

pvp_achievable.description: The gate's binary verdict for this segment. 'yes' requires exemplar; 'no' requires gap.

revised.description: True only when pvp_achievable is 'yes' AND the message needed the single revision pass to clear (it cleared on the second attempt, not the first). Constitution Section 7.

allOf.description: A 'yes' carries an exemplar and no gap.
A 'no' carries a gap and no exemplar.

exemplar.description: The cohort-level evidence message proving a PVP is achievable. NOT a deliverable for scaled use. No merge fields, no account personalization, no CTA, no em-dashes, Cannonball voice. Exactly one subject line and one eyebrow line.

eyebrow_line.description: Exactly one (preview / eyebrow line). No em-dashes.

message_body.description: The one-step message. Ends on the value, carries no CTA, no em-dashes.

facts_used.description: The specific_fact values the exemplar concretely uses, with the access_class of each cited source. Lets the reviewer confirm Standard 7 type-spanning and that Standards 3/6/7 rest only on public sources.

seven_standard_check.description: All seven standards, in order, each yes/no with basis. All seven must be met for the parent verdict to be 'yes'.

override_warning.description: Required when the run was a Silver/Bronze override. The constitution Section 3 trade-off warning, attached per message.

gap.description: The gate's 'no' for a segment. A first-class output of equal standing to an exemplar, not an error. Names which standard(s) cannot be met and what input would close the gap.

failed_standards.description: The Gold Standard numbers this segment cannot clear (after the single revision pass, if one was attempted).

what_is_missing.description: The concrete gap in the artifact. Example: specific_facts carries one dated value and no named entity.

input_that_would_close_it.description: What the user would add to the FHC artifact to flip this to 'yes'.
